findings: Backend uses the model vocabulary size and HF tokenizer to build a cached GrammarCompiler.
The engine compiler is distinct from a standalone CPU conformance compiler. Neutral model warmups must use the identical constant schema before any scored native reset.
CPU schema conversion alone is insufficient; tokenizer-aware actual compile and complete matcher accept/reject checks are required.
additionalProperties:false belongs in the schema; the engine disable_additional_properties option is guidance-specific.

GenerateString prioritizes patterns over separate length constraints; its length-only branch excludes JSON escape alternatives. Therefore do not claim maxLength/pattern grammar is universally equivalent to the parser language.
The0.2.8 pattern path differs from0.1.32 by JSON-string filtering; oneOf also has disjointness handling with a fallback. Older-version caveats are not automatically current-version results.
GrammarMatcher.is_completed() distinguishes complete strings from merely accepted prefixes; use it in truncated-output tests.
